Time Series 2: ARIMA Models¶

An ARMA model explains a stationary series by its own past values and past shocks. An ARIMA model differences the series first, to handle a unit root; a seasonal ARIMA (SARIMA) adds terms at the seasonal lag. After this chapter you can fit these models by maximum likelihood, choose their orders, forecast, and check the residuals.

Every program is complete and its output is the output of that program.

The model¶

For a series x_t (after any differencing and removal of the mean) the ARMA(p, q) model is

x_t = a₁ x_{t−1} + … + a_p x_{t−p} + e_t + b₁ e_{t−1} + … + b_q e_{t−q},

with independent shocks e_t of variance σ². Seasonal terms multiply: the full autoregressive polynomial is (1 − φ₁B − …)(1 − Φ₁Bˢ − …) and the moving-average polynomial (1 + θ₁B + …)(1 + Θ₁Bˢ + …), with B the lag operator, so a model with one regular and one seasonal AR term (period 12) has coefficients at lags 1, 12 and 13 (−φΦ).

The orders are given by ArimaOptions (ar_order, diff_order, ma_order, seasonal_ar_order, seasonal_diff_order, seasonal_ma_order, seasonal_period) or by SarimaOptions in the usual letters (p, d, q, P, D, Q, s).

Option

Meaning

Default

demean

subtract the sample mean first (a free mean is estimated as well)

true

ar0, ma0, sar0, sma0, intercept0

starting values (the default start is the zero polynomial, which is valid)

zeros

exact_likelihood

exact Gaussian likelihood (Kalman filter, stationary start), or the conditional likelihood that skips the first max(p, q) observations

true

stationarity_margin

the partial autocorrelations are kept inside ±(1 − margin)

1e-6

max_iterations, max_evaluations, simplex_delta

settings of the Nelder–Mead search

800, 6000, 0.05

The search runs over the partial autocorrelations of each polynomial (through tanh), so every candidate is stationary (autoregressive) or invertible (moving average), and the whole such region is reachable. Models with exogenous regressors (fit_mle(y, x, options)) use the conditional likelihood.

ArimaFit holds ar, ma, sar, sma, beta, mean, intercept, sigma, and the methods loglik(y), loglik_per_obs(y), infer(y) (one-step prediction errors), forecast(h, y), simulate(n), score(y) and observed_inf(y) (the numerical gradient and information matrix at the fit). SarimaFit wraps an ArimaFit in core with the same methods.

Checklist¶

  1. Look at the ACF and PACF and run ADF and KPSS first (Chapter 1); difference what has a unit root.

  2. Fit a few orders and compare Akaike’s and Schwarz’s criteria; prefer the smaller model when they disagree.

  3. Check the residuals with a Ljung–Box test whose model_df equals the number of coefficients.

  4. Forecast with forecast(h, y); remember that forecasts of a stationary model revert to the mean.

  5. For seasonal data use Sarima with the seasonal period; the seasonal and regular terms multiply.
